text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's daily newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not independently verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
- The government relased a human rights report outlining human rights violations, including torture, during and after Kenneth Kaunda was president.
- Nurses in the northern town of Kitwe have called off a four-day strike for improved conditions of service, union officials said.
- A teachers' strike for more pay in the mining towns of Copperbelt Province has spread to parts of the capital, Lusaka, the teachers' union said.

- A contagious disease suspected to be cholera has broken out in a Lusaka prison where six opposition leaders, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's deputy, are detained, prison officials said. Nine inmates have so far been admitted to hospital for treatment.
